questions.question: What is an electrical insulator? Give four examples.
questions.expected_answer: An insulator is a material that does not let electricity flow through it easily. Most non-metals are insulators, such as plastic, rubber, glass, ceramic, dry wood, paper, cloth and dry air.

questions.question: Give four ways insulators are used to keep people safe.
questions.expected_answer: Plastic coats cover electrical wires and cables. Plugs, sockets, switches and appliances have plastic covers. Electricians' tools have plastic or rubber handles, and they wear rubber gloves and boots. Glass or ceramic insulators hold bare power lines on pylons so electricity does not flow down the pylon.

questions.question: Why is damaged insulation dangerous, and give three safety rules.
questions.expected_answer: If the plastic is cracked or frayed, the copper conductor is exposed, so a person who touches it can get an electric shock, and it can cause sparks and fires. Never use an appliance with a cracked plug or frayed cord, and get it repaired properly; never tape over damage; pull plugs out by the plug; never touch electrical things with wet hands; and stay far away from fallen power lines.
